Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment before the next steps:

- Use case: frontline clinical Q&A for internal triage (nurses and triage docs). Must refuse/route when asked for diagnostics or treatment plans, and always surface source citations from our internal docs.
- Throughput: ~500 requests/day initially, spiking to ~5k/day for pilot clinics.
- Latency target: 300–400ms p50 for short answers; tolerable up to 800ms for longer contextual responses.
- Data constraints: PHI may appear in prompts; we need retention controls and a clear private deployment option.

Can you send the recommended model shortlist, a suggested prompt set we can run as quick probes, and the set of safety/refusal checks you plan to run? Also please flag any quality regression risks you see based on the example prompts we shared.

Thanks — Lina
Clinical Innovation Lead
MedSigma

Lina — great to meet you and thanks for the clear summary. Quick follow-up and next steps below. I attached a short prompt set and an initial benchmark PDF from our quick probe run.

Recap + commitments:
- Shortlist (initial): redwood-1-mini (low-latency, family of distilled models), rwd-qa-3b-quant (better factuality on clinical passages after small-context fine-tune), and rwd-llm-safe-6b (more conservative safety defaults). Ben included detailed rationale in his note below.
- Prompt probes: attached medsigma_prompt_set_v1.txt — these include 18 prompts covering allowed/forbidden queries, citation requests, and edge-case PHI exposure. Please run these against your internal docs as well (we can provide a small runner).
- Safety/refusal tests: we ran an automated pass with a hand-curated refusal set; highlights are in safety_tests_snippets.txt (attached). Our initial finding: rwd-qa-3b-quant produces better citation anchoring but occasionally hallucinates on rare disease names unless lengthened context windows are provided. That’s the biggest regression risk.
- Deployment options: for PHI we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) for the pilot. We can parallel test Hosted with strict retention offloading to validate latency first.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to share model-specific perf/cost tradeoffs and recommended default config (batching/KV cache) — by EOD tomorrow.
2) Grace to propose a safety probe matrix and a short canary rollout plan (1 clinic -> 3 clinics) — by Tue 11/23.
3) MedSigma to run attached prompt set against their canonical KB and share 10 representative failures/examples.
4) Quick 30-min sync to review probe outputs and pick a model for a 2-week pilot (recommended window: 11/30–12/14).

If OK I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering to prepare a small runner and a Drive link for secure upload.

Adding model / config specifics and the tradeoffs we discussed on the call:

- redwood-1-mini (lowest cost/latency): pros = ~220ms p50 on our smallest GPU profile, good for short factoid Q&A; cons = weaker citation fidelity on long-context retrievals, likely need external verification for any safety-critical content.
- rwd-qa-3b-quant (balanced): pros = highest passage-level factuality in our quick probe, naturally better with a 2–4k context window; cons = ~2x cost vs mini and p95 latency can hit 700–850ms under small clusters without KV caching.
- rwd-llm-safe-6b (safety-tuned): pros = much stronger refusal behavior on prompts that request diagnosis/treatment; cons = more conservative — may decline borderline allowed queries (requires prompt tuning).

Recommended default config for pilot:
- Model: rwd-qa-3b-quant (pilot) with a canary on redwood-1-mini for high-traffic clinics.
- Quantization: 4-bit for dedicated pools (saves ~45% memory) — we validated no major degradation in citation retrieval during probes.
- KV caching: enabled with 30-minute TTL for follow-ups in the same session — saves ~18% tokens on our probe workload.
- Safety layer: pre-filter + refusal scaffolding + a chained-verification step that forces the model to return source snippets when confidence < 0.6.

Quality regression risks to watch (from our probe runs):
- Named-entity hallucinations when KB has sparse entries (rare diseases, drug combos).
- Compression-induced loss when we aggressively batch and shorten contexts.
- Temperature drift from prompt templates if we use inline instruction variants across clinics.

I’ll prepare a short matrix with expected latencies and estimated monthly cost for both Hosted and Dedicated profiles and share by tomorrow morning.

— Ben
